prompt.context_jp: 資料に落としていた視線を上げた瞬間、鶸田の目に、鷹野の指がつまんだひとつの菓子＿飛び込んできた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 鷹野の指がつまんだひとつの菓子＿飛び込んできた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this moment of sudden visual discovery.

feedback.correct_en: The candy is new information that abruptly enters Hiwada's field of vision — classic が for a freshly perceived subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark the candy as an already-established topic, which it isn't. を is wrong because 飛び込む here is intransitive (the candy itself jumps into view).

contrast_examples.jp: 急に猫が飛び出してきた。
contrast_examples.en: A cat suddenly jumped out (new to the scene).

contrast_examples.jp: その猫はいつもそこにいる。
contrast_examples.en: That cat (already known) is always there.

prompt.context_jp: 朱雀部長の発言について鴫石が引用している場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: この会社には「ありがとう」＿足りない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this diagnostic statement about the company.

feedback.correct_en: 〜が足りない identifies what's missing as new information — it's an existence/quantity claim. が is standard with 足りない in this diagnostic frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 「ありがとう」 a contrastive topic (as opposed to something else), which doesn't match the complaint that gratitude in general is lacking.

contrast_examples.jp: お金は足りているが、時間がない。
contrast_examples.en: Money is fine, but there's no time (contrastive).

prompt.context_jp: 鳩山さんが鷹野に感謝しすぎだと指摘された直後、鷹野が答える。
prompt.prompt_jp: 鳩山さん＿1日10回以上 私に感謝してくれています。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits Takano's deadpan statement about Hatoyama.

feedback.correct_en: Hatoyama was just named in the previous turn, so he's the established topic. は continues that topic and sets up the comment about his behavior.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce Hatoyama as new information — jarring when he was literally the subject of the preceding question.

contrast_examples.jp: 田中さんは毎日来ます。
contrast_examples.en: Tanaka (as for him) comes every day.

contrast_examples.jp: 誰が来たの？—田中さんが来ました。

prompt.context_jp: 烏森が、なぜ鶸田と鷹野が担当なのかを説明する。
prompt.prompt_jp: その部のいちばん若手＿担当することになってるんだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this rule-statement about who does it.

feedback.correct_en: This is an exhaustive-listing/identification が — it specifies exactly who (the youngest) is the one assigned. The question behind it is 'who does it?'
feedback.incorrect_en: は would weakly topicalize 'the youngest' as if there were other groups to contrast — but the point is pinpointing them as the sole designee.

contrast_examples.en: The eldest son is the one who inherits the house.

contrast_examples.jp: 長男は家を継ぐが、次男は出ていく。
contrast_examples.en: The eldest inherits, but the second son leaves (contrast).

prompt.context_jp: 鴫石が、燕谷の仕事ぶりを擁護する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 成果物＿スケジュールどおりにアップしてくれてるから 業務的には問題ないんだよね。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this defense of the remote worker.

feedback.correct_en: は sets up a contrastive topic: 'at least the deliverables (as for those) are on time' — implying other things (attendance, attitude) may not be. The next clause 業務的には confirms this contrastive framing.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark deliverables as newly introduced information, but here the speaker is sorting what's okay from what isn't — exactly what は does.

contrast_examples.en: Work (at least) he does properly (implying something else may not be).

prompt.context_jp: 雉谷が、なぜそこまで会社訪問にこだわるのかを説明する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 俺＿何事も完璧にやり遂げたいんだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this self-declaration.

feedback.correct_en: First-person self-characterization: '(as for me) I want to do everything perfectly.' は topicalizes the speaker and introduces a personal stance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 俺が would answer 'who wants to do it perfectly?' — a focus/identification reading that doesn't fit a self-introduction of one's values.

contrast_examples.jp: 私はコーヒーが好きだ。

contrast_examples.en: I'll be the one to do it (identifying who).

prompt.context_jp: 国男が、朱雀の会社の立地自慢を一蹴する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 今どき 立地＿ステータスにならないし。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this dismissive counter-point.

feedback.correct_en: Contrastive は: 'location (unlike other things) isn't a status marker anymore.' The speaker is picking out 立地 to downgrade it, which は handles.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 立地 as the newly identified subject, but the discourse is pushing back on the previous claim about location — a textbook は-contrast move.

contrast_examples.en: Money (as opposed to other things) isn't what matters.

prompt.context_jp: 副社長がIT導入の意義を社長に説明する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼らの提案＿ウチの会社の業務のシステム化です。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this A=B explanatory sentence.

feedback.correct_en: This is a canonical 'X は Y です' definition: 'Their proposal is systemization of our operations.' は presents the known topic and equates it with the explanation.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn it into an identifying answer to 'whose proposal is systemization?' — not the discourse move here.

contrast_examples.en: This book is an introductory text.
This book is the introductory one (identifying among many).

prompt.context_jp: サンポ導入後の職場の変化を地の文が描写する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部内では小さな貸し借り＿増えていった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this narrative report of a new trend.

feedback.correct_en: Narration introducing a new phenomenon: 'small favors (newly) began to increase.' が marks the newly-arising subject in a scene-reporting sentence.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 貸し借り a topic being discussed, but here it's being introduced into the narrative for the first time.

contrast_examples.en: Overtime (as for it) happens every month.

prompt.context_jp: 鵜飼が、鳩山の「ありがとう」を皮肉って言う引用部分。
prompt.prompt_jp: “鷹野＿役に立っているから 会社にいてもいいのだ”
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this quoted self-justification.

feedback.correct_en: Takano is the topic being evaluated: '(as for Takano,) she's useful, so she may stay.' は sets her up as the subject of judgment.
feedback.incorrect_en: 鷹野が役に立っている would answer 'who is useful?' — focus/identification. Here the point is about Takano's qualification, not picking her out among others.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は優秀だから採用された。
contrast_examples.en: He is excellent, so he was hired (characterization).

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚社長が九州の取引を断る理由を述べる。
prompt.prompt_jp: マメに足を運ぶの＿難しい。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in this 〜のは〜 evaluation pattern.

feedback.correct_en: の nominalizes the action, then は topicalizes it: 'as for frequently going, it's difficult.' This is the standard 〜のは〜 evaluative pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが難しい is grammatical in other frames (e.g., 〜のが得意) but here the sentence is making a general judgment about the activity, which calls for は.

contrast_examples.en: I like swimming (preference pattern uses が).

prompt.context_jp: 雉谷が貝塚製菓について評する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 貝塚製菓＿体質古いんで 契約ムズいと思いますけど。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames the client company as the topic.

feedback.correct_en: The client has just been named in the previous turns; は picks it up as the topic for a characterization ('as for Kaizuka, the culture is old').
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the company as new, but it's already on the table — and the sentence is a property-attribution, not an identification.

contrast_examples.en: That company is old-fashioned (characterizing a known topic).

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚社長の方針を副社長が代弁する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 直接 会える人としか 仕事＿しない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in this restrictive-policy statement.

feedback.correct_en: With a negative-polarity restriction like 〜としか〜ない, 仕事は highlights 仕事 as the scope being contrastively restricted. 仕事は しない pairs naturally with 〜しか.
feedback.incorrect_en: を is grammatically possible as a plain object marker but loses the contrastive 'as for work, (only with those people)' nuance that fits the policy framing.

prompt.context_jp: 鶸田が会社訪問の担当を断る言い訳をする。
prompt.prompt_jp: 今 初めて 大きい案件＿任されてて それで手いっぱいなんだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the object of 任される (be entrusted with).

feedback.correct_en: 任される takes the entrusted thing as its direct object with を, even in the passive form: 案件を任される = 'be entrusted with a project.'
feedback.incorrect_en: に marks the agent (誰に任される), not the item entrusted. が would try to make 案件 the subject, but Hiwada is the one receiving the task.

contrast_examples.jp: 大事な仕事を任された。
contrast_examples.en: I was entrusted with an important job.

prompt.context_jp: 鴫石がサンキューポイントの仕組みを説明する。
prompt.prompt_jp: このアプリを立ち上げて 相手＿ポイントつけることができるんだって。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the recipient of the points.

feedback.correct_en: に marks the recipient/goal of an action — here, the person who receives the points. 相手にポイントをつける = 'assign points to the other person.'
feedback.incorrect_en: を would make 相手 the direct object of つける, which collides with ポイント already filling that slot. で would read as 'using the person as a means,' which is nonsensical.

contrast_examples.jp: 友達にメッセージを送る。
contrast_examples.en: I send a message to a friend.

contrast_examples.jp: ペンでメッセージを書く。
contrast_examples.en: I write a message with a pen (means).

prompt.context_jp: 鴫石がアドレスホッパーについて説明する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 特定の住居とか持たずに 移動しながら生活してる人のこと。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that would complete '移動しながら生活' if you wanted to add 'spend one's life traveling around the country' — pick the correct particle for the direct object of a verb like 送る (to lead a life).

choices.text: を (全国を移動しながら生活を送る)
に (全国に移動しながら生活に送る)
で (全国で移動しながら生活で送る)

feedback.correct_en: を marks both 全国 as the area traversed (motion-through を) and 生活 as the direct object of 送る. Both uses of を are standard here.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a destination (one point), not continuous traversal. で would mark a location where an action happens, which doesn't match 'moving through' or 送る (lead a life).

prompt.context_jp: 章の冒頭、営業部の朝の描写。
prompt.prompt_jp: 朝の営業部＿、書類とタイピングの音で満ちていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames this opening scene.

feedback.correct_en: Opening descriptions of a setting use は to establish the scene as the topic — 'As for the morning sales department, it was filled with...'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the office as freshly spotted information, more like a sudden sighting. For a wide-angle scene opener, は is natural.

contrast_examples.jp: ふと見ると、男が立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: Suddenly, a man was standing there (new appearance).

prompt.context_jp: 鵜飼がサンポ制度を批判する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 会社にお膳立てされて感謝するって なんか ＿＿みたいで 気持ち悪くないですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that best captures the 'phony/cozy' feeling Ukai objects to.

feedback.correct_en: なれ合い carries a negative nuance of 'cozy, back-scratching collusion' — exactly the sham intimacy Ukai is complaining about.
feedback.incorrect_en: 触れ合い is warm/positive contact, 話し合い is a neutral discussion — neither captures the 'staged, chummy, creepy' tone the speaker intends.

contrast_examples.jp: 政治家同士のなれ合い。

contrast_examples.en: Warm interaction between parent and child.

prompt.context_jp: 鳩山が鵜飼の反発を軽くあしらう。
prompt.prompt_jp: そんなムキになって反発するほうが ＿＿ぞ！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the adjective Hatoyama uses to call Ukai's reaction childish.

feedback.correct_en: 大人げない means 'unbecoming of an adult / immature,' which is the dig Hatoyama lands.
feedback.incorrect_en: 大人っぽい and 大人びた both mean 'adult-like' in a positive sense — the opposite of what the speaker wants to say.

contrast_examples.jp: そんなことで怒るなんて大人げない。
contrast_examples.en: Getting mad over that is childish.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女は年の割に大人っぽい。
contrast_examples.en: She seems grown-up for her age.

prompt.context_jp: 鶸田がリモート会議の苦手さを語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: ビデオで撮られてるっていうだけでも ＿＿あるし みんなにミュートとかされたら 反応分からなくて…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the phrase that fits 'feels nerve-wracking.'

feedback.correct_en: 緊張感がある = 'there's tension/stress.' This matches Hiwada being nervous just from being on camera.
feedback.incorrect_en: 責任感 is 'sense of responsibility' and 達成感 is 'sense of accomplishment' — both are positive/duty-related and don't fit the complaint about being on camera.

contrast_examples.jp: 試合前は緊張感がある。
仕事が終わって達成感がある。
contrast_examples.en: After finishing work there's a sense of accomplishment.

prompt.context_jp: 雉谷が会社訪問の良さを語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 未来に希望を持った学生たちと話すとさ…なんか 心が＿＿ような気持ちになるんだよな。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that completes 'feel one's spirit cleansed.'

feedback.correct_en: 心が洗われる is a fixed expression meaning 'to feel refreshed/cleansed in spirit,' commonly used for pure, moving experiences.
feedback.incorrect_en: 心が磨かれる exists but refers to character-polishing through training, not refreshing feelings. 心が拭かれる is not an idiomatic collocation.

contrast_examples.jp: 美しい景色に心が洗われた。
contrast_examples.en: The beautiful scenery cleansed my spirit.

contrast_examples.jp: 厳しい修行で心が磨かれる。

prompt.context_jp: 燕谷がオフィスに行かない理由を主張する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 飲み会だとか 会社の＿＿行事だとか 仕事以外の人間関係が煩わしいだけじゃないですか。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the adjective that captures 'pointless/barren.'

feedback.correct_en: 不毛な means 'barren / fruitless / pointless' — perfect for dismissing company events as wastes of time.
feedback.incorrect_en: 不便な is 'inconvenient' (practical complaint), 不安な is 'anxious' (emotional state) — neither captures the 'yields nothing worthwhile' nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 朱雀の叔母が、息子を押しつける電話をかけてくる。
prompt.prompt_jp: だから あんたの会社ぐらいで ＿＿もらいたくて。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the idiom meaning 'settle for / strike a deal.'

feedback.correct_en: 手を打つ (colloquially 手ぇ打つ) means 'settle a matter / strike a deal' — the aunt wants to settle for Suzaku's company as a landing spot.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手を振る is 'wave,' 手を上げる is 'raise one's hand / give up (depending on context)' — neither carries the 'cut a deal' sense.

contrast_examples.jp: この条件で手を打とう。

prompt.context_jp: 朱雀部長がサンキューポイント導入を頼んできた背景。
prompt.prompt_jp: なんか 家族への＿＿のためだって。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun that fits 'making amends to one's family.'

feedback.correct_en: 償い means 'atonement / making amends,' which fits a workaholic dad trying to compensate his family with a Korea trip.
feedback.incorrect_en: 祝い is 'celebration' and 占い is 'fortune-telling' — unrelated to the apology/compensation framing.

prompt.context_jp: 梟井がサンポをせしめる白鳥の様子に呆れる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 出た出た サンポの＿＿。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun meaning 'exploitation / shakedown.'

feedback.correct_en: 搾取 means 'exploitation / squeezing something out of someone' — exactly the critical label put on Shiratori's point-grabbing habit.
feedback.incorrect_en: 収穫 is 'harvest (crops/results)' and 採取 is 'collecting (specimens),' both neutral — neither carries the 'extraction at someone's expense' nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 雉谷が自分の信条を語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 俺は何事も完璧に＿＿たいんだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'see through to completion.'

feedback.correct_en: やり遂げる = 'complete something all the way through, see it through to the end.' Pairs naturally with 完璧に.
feedback.incorrect_en: やり直す is 'redo,' やり過ごす is 'let something pass / shrug it off' — opposite of 'finishing perfectly.'

contrast_examples.jp: 最後まで仕事をやり遂げた。
contrast_examples.en: I saw the job through to the end.

contrast_examples.jp: 面倒な客をやり過ごす。

prompt.context_jp: 鳩山がサンポ制度を建設的に捉える発言をする場面での自然な言い方。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural when conceding 'it might be a bit embarrassing, but...'?

choices.text: 多少 こう テレくさい所はあるけどさ
多少 こう テレくさい所がいるけどさ

feedback.correct_en: 〜所がある is the standard collocation for 'there's an aspect of ~'. Hatoyama's hedging naturally uses ある.
feedback.incorrect_en: いる is for animate existence (people/animals), so 所がいる is ungrammatical in this abstract 'aspect' sense.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼には優しい所がある。

contrast_examples.en: There are students in the classroom (animate).

prompt.context_jp: 烏森が燕谷に、慣例を伝える丁寧な言い方。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural in a polite business explanation?

choices.text: 毎年 その課のいちばん若い方に 担当していただくのが決まりなんです
毎年 その課のいちばん若い方を 担当してもらうのが決まりなんです

feedback.correct_en: 担当していただく with に (marking the person doing the favor for us) + humble いただく is the smooth, polite phrasing a HR rep would use.
feedback.incorrect_en: を担当してもらう drops the honorific register and treats the person as a direct object of the favor, which clashes with 若い方 (polite reference).

contrast_examples.jp: 先生にご指導いただく。
友達に手伝ってもらう。

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚社長が九州の案件を断る指示。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is a more natural business refusal?

choices.text: 丁重にお断りしてください
丁重に断ってあげてください

feedback.correct_en: お断りする is the humble form used in business for declining — paired with 丁重に ('politely/respectfully') it's the standard phrasing for a formal refusal.
feedback.incorrect_en: 断ってあげる implies doing the other party a favor by refusing, which is condescending and inappropriate for a business turndown.

contrast_examples.jp: ご提案は丁重にお断りしました。
彼女に代わって断ってあげた。
contrast_examples.en: I turned them down on her behalf (favor nuance).

prompt.context_jp: 鶸田が、日程変更を頼めない理由を鳩山に説明する。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural when reporting what the client said?

choices.text: 何度も 今日以外は 日程はないって言われてたんで
何度も 今日以外は 日程はないって言ってたんで

feedback.correct_en: 言われていた (passive) is natural when reporting what you were told by the client — it keeps the speaker as the recipient of the message.
feedback.incorrect_en: 言ってた (active) with no subject reads as if someone unspecified was saying it, which weakens the 'the client told me repeatedly' point Hiwada is making.

contrast_examples.jp: 部長にそう言われていた。
contrast_examples.en: I had been told so by the manager.

prompt.context_jp: 鳩山がサンポ制度について聞いたことを伝える。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural for 'I've heard other companies do this too'?

choices.text: ほかの会社でも やってるって聞いたことあります
ほかの会社にも やってるって聞いたことあります

feedback.correct_en: でも marks 'at/in other companies as well' — the location where the activity happens. やる is an action that takes place somewhere, so で is correct.
feedback.incorrect_en: に marks destination/goal, not the site of an ongoing activity. 会社にやる would imply 'do it toward the company,' which doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.en: They sell it abroad too (location of action).
